definitions.explanation: Worrying about something that hasn't happened yet and may never happen. Borrowing trouble.

examples.japanese: それは{取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}だよ。
{取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}をしても{仕方|しかた}がない。
examples.english: There's no point in worrying about things that haven't happened.

examples.japanese: {心配|しんぱい}していたけど、{結局|けっきょく}{取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}だった。
examples.english: I was worried, but in the end it turned out to be needless anxiety.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used to reassure someone who is worrying unnecessarily, or to reflect on one's own past worries that turned out to be unfounded. Often appears as {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}をする (to worry needlessly) or {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}だった (it was needless worry).

ETYMOLOGY:
From {取|と}り{越|こ}す (to bring forward, to anticipate) + {苦労|くろう} (hardship, worry). Literally "suffering brought forward" — worrying about something before it happens.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}をする: to worry needlessly
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}に{終|お}わる: to end up being needless worry
